name: Computer Applications and IoT
objectives: Solve basic information systems problems using MS Office products.
Communicate in a business environment using MS Office.
Describe and analyze computer hardware and software.
outcomes: CO1 Solve basic information systems problems using MS Office products appropriate for the solution.
CO2 Communicate in a business environment using the MS Office product.
CO3 Understanding DOS commands and Linux programming.
CO4 Describe and analyze computer hardware and software.
CO5 Understanding the concepts of IOT.
rule: 8 experiments as listed in the official table

exps.title: 1 Experiments on dismantling of PC: Dismantling the system unit, recognize all major components inside a PC, describe function of each component and define the relationship of internal components.
exps.aim: Open a system unit, identify components and describe their functions and relationships.
exps.apparatus: Screwdriver set, anti-static wrist strap, PC cabinet
exps.formula: Data flow: input → CPU + RAM (motherboard) → storage/output
viva: Motherboard, CPU, RAM, SMPS, HDD/SSD, graphics/network cards, cooling fan.
Converts AC mains to regulated DC voltages for the components.

exps.title: 2(a) Experiments on DOS: Perform these internal commands: DIR, TYPE, DEL, ERASE, MD, CD, COPY, RMDIR, VER, DATE, TIME, PATH, CLS, RMDIR, VER, DATE, TIME, PATH, CLS, BREAK, SET, EXIT.
exps.aim: Run DOS internal commands at the command prompt.
exps.formula: Internal commands are built into COMMAND.COM; e.g. MD dir, CD dir, COPY src dest
viva: One built into the command interpreter, needing no separate file.
Lists files and folders of the current directory.

exps.title: 2(b) Perform external commands: APPEND, CHKDISK, ATTRIB, SYS, EDIT.
exps.formula: External commands are separate program files, e.g. ATTRIB +R file sets read-only
viva: Difference between internal and external commands?
External commands are stored as separate files on disk and loaded when run.
Displays or changes file attributes (read-only, hidden, system, archive).

exps.title: 3(a) Experiments on system utilities: Explore and describe some system utility like regedit, memory portioning, control panel, window tools.
exps.aim: Explore system utilities and describe their functions.
exps.apparatus: Windows PC, regedit, Disk Management, Control Panel
exps.formula: Utilities: regedit (registry), Disk Management (partitions), Control Panel (settings)
viva: A hierarchical database of Windows configuration settings.
Dividing a physical disk into separate logical volumes.

exps.title: 3(b) List various keys in registry and perform experiments to back up a key in registry using regedit.
exps.aim: List the root registry keys and export a key as a backup.
exps.formula: Root keys: HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT, HKEY_CURRENT_USER, HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE, HKEY_USERS, HKEY_CURRENT_CONFIG; File > Export
viva: How do you back up a key?
Select it in regedit and use File > Export to save a .reg file.
Wrong edits can make the system unstable.

exps.title: 4(a) Experiments on Linux: Perform an experiment to install any rpm or debian linux distribution.
exps.aim: Install an RPM-based (Fedora/CentOS) or Debian-based (Ubuntu) Linux distribution.
exps.apparatus: Bootable USB/ISO, VirtualBox or spare PC
exps.formula: Steps: boot media → choose language → partition disk → create user → install
viva: Give examples of rpm and debian based distros.
The core of the OS managing hardware, processes and memory.

exps.title: 4(b) Install rpm and deb packages.
exps.aim: Install software using rpm/dpkg package tools.
exps.formula: rpm -ivh pkg.rpm ; dpkg -i pkg.deb ; apt install / yum install

exps.title: 4(c) Perform these commands in linux: chmod, su, chown, chgrp, ls, mkdir, pwd, date, who, find, uname, wc, ifconfig.
exps.formula: chmod 755 file (rwxr-xr-x); ls -l; find . -name f; wc -l file
viva: Owner read/write; group and others read only.

exps.title: 4(d) Create, open, edit, view file in linux.
exps.aim: Create and edit files using shell commands and editors.
exps.formula: touch f; cat > f; vi f; cat f; less f
viva: How do you save and quit in vi?

exps.title: 4(e) Create user and group through CLI.
exps.aim: Create users and groups from the command line.
exps.formula: groupadd grp ; useradd -m -G grp user ; passwd user

exps.title: 5(a) Experiments on MS Office Word/Open Office Writer: Create an office writer document and using tables distinguish between different types of memories.
exps.aim: Insert a table comparing types of memory (RAM, ROM, cache, secondary).
exps.formula: Insert > Table; rows = memory types, columns = speed, volatility, use
viva: How to insert a table in Word?
Insert > Table and choose rows and columns.
Yes, it loses data when power is off.

exps.title: 5(b) Draft a letter asking for quotations of different peripheral devices for your computer lab and mail the letter using mail merge in MS Word/open office writer.
exps.aim: Write a quotation request letter and merge it with a recipient list.
exps.apparatus: MS Word / LibreOffice Writer, data source (Excel/CSV)
exps.formula: Mail merge = main document + data source + merge fields
viva: Combining a template letter with a data list to make personalised copies.
Placeholders such as «Name» replaced by data source values.

exps.title: 5(c) Create a MS Word/open office writer document and implement macro function.
exps.aim: Record and run a macro to automate a task.
exps.formula: View > Macros > Record Macro > perform actions > Stop > Run
viva: A recorded or coded sequence of actions that can be replayed.
Which language does MS Office use for macros?

exps.title: 5(d) Create a template and draw a basic block diagram of computer & using graphs compare the performance of different laptop/notebook PC.
exps.aim: Save a document template, draw a block diagram and add a chart comparing laptops.
exps.apparatus: MS Word / LibreOffice Writer, shapes and chart tools
exps.formula: Block diagram: Input → CPU (ALU, CU) + Memory → Output
viva: A preset document layout that can be reused.
Name the parts of the CPU.
Arithmetic logic unit, control unit and registers.

exps.title: 6 Experiments on MS Office Excel/Open Office Calc: Create a database of students, which contains marks obtained by students of a class in different subjects and then calculate maximum, minimum, average and sum of marks in each subject. Also calculate % of each student using functions and formulas in MS Excel/Open Office Calc; also draw pie chart and bar graph.
exps.aim: Build a marks sheet and compute MAX, MIN, AVERAGE, SUM, percentage, and draw charts.
viva: Difference between relative and absolute reference?
Relative shifts on copying (A1); absolute stays fixed ($A$1).

exps.title: 7 Experiments on MS Office Power Point/Open Office Impress: Make a simple presentation on your college, use 3D effects, animation on network topologies.
exps.aim: Create a slide presentation with 3D effects and animated network topology diagrams.
exps.formula: Topologies: bus, star, ring, mesh, tree; Insert > Shapes; Animations tab
viva: Bus, star, ring, mesh and tree.

exps.title: 8(a) Experiments on IoT: Basic Components of IOT, Interaction with the Internet, Major Components of IoT devices: Control Units, Sensors, Communication modules, Power Sources, Communication Technologies: RFID, Bluetooth, Zigbee, WiFi, RF Links, Mobile Internet, Wired Communication. Familiarization of Arduino/Raspberry Pi and perform necessary software installation.
exps.aim: Study IoT components and communication technologies; get familiar with Arduino/Raspberry Pi and install the required software.
exps.apparatus: Arduino board / Raspberry Pi, USB cable, Arduino IDE / Raspberry Pi OS
exps.formula: IoT stack: sensors → controller → communication module → cloud/internet
viva: Sensors, control unit, communication module and power source.
Arduino is a microcontroller board; Raspberry Pi is a single-board computer running an OS.

exps.title: 8(b) To interface LED/Buzzer with Arduino / Raspberry Pi and write a program to turn on LED for 1 sec.
exps.aim: Connect an LED/buzzer to a digital pin and turn it on for 1 second.
exps.apparatus: Arduino/Raspberry Pi, LED, 220 Ω resistor, breadboard, jumper wires
exps.formula: Arduino: pinMode(13,OUTPUT); digitalWrite(13,HIGH); delay(1000); digitalWrite(13,LOW); series resistor R = (Vs − VLED)/I
viva: Why a resistor with the LED?
To limit current and avoid burning the LED.
